newsitem.title: USA: Internet trends could lead to downsizing - experts.
newsitem.headline: Internet trends could lead to downsizing - experts.

text.p: The World Wide Web's increasing role as a capitalist tool could bring about a new era of corporate downsizing, as companies move toward Internet-based automation methods designed to slash payrolls and other costs, industry executives say.

While the widespread layoffs of recent years continue to spawn job insecurity in the workplace, the computer industry has begun pushing new Web-based software products that allow companies to make some traditional office jobs obsolete.

A leading product line is an Internet-technology called "Intranet," which allows companies to set up internal Websites where employees can find up-to-date information about topics such as health and pension plans.

So-called "Extranet" products also can be used to create external Internet-links between companies for the purpose of executing routine business transactions otherwise carried out by paper-based purchase and shipment order systems.
"You can literally remove the people who have been answering the phone in the past," Microsoft Corp Chief Operating Officer Bob Herbold said.
"All those phone calls, all those human beings involved, all the paperwork involved can disappear," he said at the Internet Commerce Expo in a keynote speech.

A senior executive with International Business Machines Corp said the government of Singapore was able to reduce manpower 45 percent and slash costs 62 percent in some departments after moving suppliers into just such a system.

Meanwhile, computer executives say a cadre of corporations ranging from airlines and automotive companies to consumer product makers and railroads are moving steadily to take advantage of the potential benefits.

The Internet has yet to overcome the legal, regulatory and security hurdles blocking it from reaching critical mass as a site for electronic commerce. But industry executives remain convinced it will bring fundamental change to the world economy, possibly in only a few years.

"Just as the Industrial Revolution changed manufacturing capacity, the Internet will change distribution. Middle men and middle-level companies will be eliminated and most companies in an industrial economy are middle-level," said Shikhar Ghosh, chairman of the Cambridge, Mass.-based software company Open Market Inc.

But while some experts warn the Internet could lead to a new period of economic dislocation, many say economic growth resulting from the new efficiency of electronic dealing would more than make up for initial job losses.
"It's less an issue of eliminating jobs than it is an issue of making people more effective," said Randall Whiting, president of the Internet industry association, CommerceNet.
"There would be so many more business opportunities that overall, net employment would rise."
